chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Makhlad al-Sarrāj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Ismail Haqeeba and Al-Harith al-Nasri: 'Seek out for me a slave girl from the one they call Kadbanouj, to be with Umm Farwa.' So they pointed us to a slave girl of a man from the al-Sarrajeen who had given birth to a son for him, and her son had died. So they informed him of her news. So he ordered them, and they bought her, and her name was Rasala, so he changed her name and called her Salma, and Salim, her master, married her, and she is the mother of Al-Husayn ibn Salim.
ai.seo_question: Who was Salma, the mother of Al-Husayn ibn Salim, and how was she acquired by the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) acquisition of the slave girl Rasala, whom he renamed Salma and married to his freedman Salim, thereby establishing the lineage of Al-Husayn ibn Salim, a prominent narrator of hadith. This narrative illustrates the practical social dynamics of the Imam’s household, where freed slaves could marry into the family structure, blurring the lines between servitude and kinship in the context of early Shia scholarly transmission.
